title: Computing 2000–2009
tagline: Broadband, mobile and the cloud begin.
source: Generated from “Timeline of computing 2000–2009” on Wikipedia; each event links to its source article.

events.title: AMD released an Athlon clocked at 1 GHz
events.text: AMD released an Athlon clocked at 1 GHz.

events.title: IBM delivers the ASCI White supercomputer to the U
events.text: IBM delivers the ASCI White supercomputer to the U.S. Department of Energy. This supercomputer was capable of performing 12.3 teraflops, making it the world's fastest at the time.

events.title: Microsoft releases Windows 2000
events.text: Microsoft releases Windows 2000.

events.title: RSA Security released their RSA algorithm into the public domain, in a
events.text: RSA Security released their RSA algorithm into the public domain, in advance of the US patent (#4,405,829) expiring on September 20 of the same year. Following the relaxation of the US government restrictions earlier in the year (January 14) this rem

events.title: The US Government announces that restrictions on exporting cryptograph
events.text: The US Government announces that restrictions on exporting cryptography are being relaxed (although not removed). This allows many US companies to stop the long running process of having to create US and international copies of their software.

events.title: Apple released macOS (as Mac OS X)
events.text: Apple released macOS (as Mac OS X). This was a new operating system derived from NeXTSTEP, using Darwin as its kernel, an Open Source operating system based on BSD. This replaced the "classic" Mac OS for its Mac computers. Mac OS X finally gave Mac u

events.title: Microsoft released Windows XP, based on Windows 2000 and Windows NT ke
events.text: Microsoft released Windows XP, based on Windows 2000 and Windows NT kernel. Windows XP introduces a heavily redesigned GUI and brings the NT kernel to the consumer market.

events.title: The Agile Manifesto, which crystallised and named a growing trend towa
events.text: The Agile Manifesto, which crystallised and named a growing trend towards more "agile" processes in software development, was released. The perceived success of agile project management led to agile approaches such as Scrum later being used as a gene

events.title: Blender, a 3D graphics software package, becomes open-source software
events.text: Blender, a 3D graphics software package, becomes open-source software after a crowdfunding campaign successfully raises €100,000.

events.title: United Linux officially formed
events.text: United Linux officially formed.

events.title: Intel releases the Pentium M for notebooks and the Centrino mobile pla
events.text: Intel releases the Pentium M for notebooks and the Centrino mobile platform. The Pentium M delivers similar or higher performance than the Pentium 4-M while consuming less power.

events.title: SCO Group announces it would sue IBM for US$1 billion
events.text: SCO Group announces it would sue IBM for US$1 billion. The claim is that Linux contains code inserted by IBM that was the copyrighted property of SCO (see SCO v. IBM).

events.title: Nintendo releases the Nintendo DS, introducing dual screens and touchs
events.text: Nintendo releases the Nintendo DS, introducing dual screens and touchscreen technology to handheld gaming.

events.title: Sony released Librié EBR-1000EP in Japan, the first e-book reader with
events.text: Sony released Librié EBR-1000EP in Japan, the first e-book reader with an E Ink electronic paper display.

events.title: Apple announces they are going to use Intel processors in upcoming Mac
events.text: Apple announces they are going to use Intel processors in upcoming Macintosh computers.

events.title: Jef Raskin, who in 1979 envisioned and established the Macintosh proje
events.text: Jef Raskin, who in 1979 envisioned and established the Macintosh project at Apple Computer, dies at the age of 61.

events.title: Nokia announces the Nokia 770 Internet Tablet, the first device runnin
events.text: Nokia announces the Nokia 770 Internet Tablet, the first device running Maemo.

events.title: Google announces acquisition of YouTube in $1
events.text: Google announces acquisition of YouTube in $1.65 billion deal, recognizing the growing importance of video content on the internet.

events.title: Intel releases the Core 2 processor
events.text: Intel releases the Core 2 processor.

events.title: Researchers create experimental processor that operates at higher than
events.text: Researchers create experimental processor that operates at higher than 500 GHz when cryogenically frozen.

events.title: Twitter is launched, introducing a new platform for microblogging and
events.text: Twitter is launched, introducing a new platform for microblogging and social interaction.

events.title: Asus announces the first Asus Eee PC, launching the netbook category o
events.text: Asus announces the first Asus Eee PC, launching the netbook category of mobile computers. It initially ran Linux; later models also offered a choice of Windows.

events.title: Blu-ray wins the high definition optical disc format war against HD DV
events.text: Blu-ray wins the high definition optical disc format war against HD DVD, becoming the industry standard for high-definition media.

events.title: The first version of Android was introduced by Google
events.text: The first version of Android was introduced by Google.

events.title: Facebook overtakes MySpace in America
events.text: Facebook overtakes MySpace in America.

events.title: The online currency Bitcoin is released
events.text: The online currency Bitcoin is released.
